citeinfo.title: Long-term monotonic trends in annual and monthly streamflow metrics at streamgages in the United States (ver. 2.0, October 2024)

descript.abstract:
The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Water Resources Mission Area (WMA) is working to address a need to understand where the Nation is experiencing water shortages or surpluses relative to the demand for water need by delivering routine assessments of water supply and demand and an understanding of the natural and human factors affecting the balance between supply and demand. A key part of these national assessments is identifying long-term trends in water availability, including groundwater and surface water quantity, quality, and use.
This data release contains Mann-Kendall monotonic trend analyses for 18 observed annual and monthly streamflow metrics at 6,347 U.S. Geological Survey streamgages located in the conterminous United States, Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico. Streamflow metrics include annual mean flow, maximum 1-day and 7-day flows, minimum 7-day and 30-day flows, and the date of the center of volume (the date on which 50% of the annual flow has passed by a gage), along with the mean flow for each month of the year. Annual streamflow metrics are computed from mean daily discharge records at U.S. Geological Survey streamgages that are publicly available from the National Water Information System (NWIS). Trend analyses are computed using annual streamflow metrics computed through climate year 2022 (April 2022- March 2023) for low-flow metrics and water year 2022 (October 2021 - September 2022) for all other metrics. Trends at each site are available for up to four different periods: (i) the longest possible period that meets completeness criteria at each site, (ii) 1980-2020, (iii) 1990-2020, (iv) 2000-2020. Annual metric time series analyzed for trends must have 80 percent complete records during fixed periods. In addition, each of these time series must have 80 percent complete records during their first and last decades. All longest possible period time series must be at least 10 years long and have annual metric values for at least 80% of the years running from 2013 to 2022.
This data release provides the following five CSV output files along with a model archive:
(1) streamflow_trend_results.csv - contains test results of all trend analyses with each row representing one unique combination of (i) NWIS streamgage identifiers, (ii) metric (computed using Oct 1 - Sep 30 water years except for low-flow metrics computed using climate years (Apr 1 - Mar 31), (iii) trend periods of interest (longest possible period through 2022, 1980-2020, 1990-2020, 2000-2020) and (iv) records containing either the full trend period or only a portion of the trend period following substantial increases in cumulative upstream reservoir storage capacity. This is an output from the final process step (#5) of the workflow.
(2) streamflow_trend_trajectories_with_confidence_bands.csv - contains annual trend trajectories estimated using Theil-Sen regression, which estimates the median of the probability distribution of a metric for a given year, along with 90 percent confidence intervals (5th and 95h percentile values). This is an output from the final process step (#5) of the workflow.
(3) streamflow_trend_screening_all_steps.csv - contains the screening results of all 7,873 streamgages initially considered as candidate sites for trend analysis and identifies the screens that prevented some sites from being included in the Mann-Kendall trend analysis.
(4) all_site_year_metrics.csv - contains annual time series values of streamflow metrics computed from mean daily discharge data at 7,873 candidate sites. This is an output of Process Step 1 in the workflow.
(5) all_site_year_filters.csv - contains information about the completeness and quality of daily mean discharge at each streamgage during each year (water year, climate year, and calendar year). This is also an output of Process Step 1 in the workflow and is combined with all_site_year_metrics.csv in Process Step 2.
In addition, a .zip file contains a model archive for reproducing the trend results using R 4.4.1 statistical software. See the README file contained in the model archive for more information.
Caution must be exercised when utilizing monotonic trend analyses conducted over periods of up to several decades (and in some places longer ones) due to the potential for confounding deterministic gradual trends with multi-decadal climatic fluctuations. In addition, trend results are available for post-reservoir construction periods within the four trend periods described above to avoid including abrupt changes arising from the construction of larger reservoirs in periods for which gradual monotonic trends are computed. Other abrupt changes, such as changes to water withdrawals and wastewater return flows, or episodic disturbances with multi-year recovery periods, such as wildfires, are not evaluated. Sites with pronounced abrupt changes or other non-monotonic trajectories of change may require more sophisticated trend analyses than those presented in this data release.
descript.purpose: Daily mean discharge data were collected to estimate annual trends in 18 different streamflow metrics at sites in the conterminous United States, Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico. These data were collected to assist water resources planners and managers in considering changing conditions in their decisions. These trend results are most appropriate to use at sites where known drivers of environmental change have prompted a gradual, monotonic increase or decrease in a streamflow metric over a defined trend period.

attracc.attraccr:
The streamflow data used in this study are comprised of daily mean discharge estimates obtained from instantaneous unit values. These unit values are typically estimated using periodically adjusted stage-discharge rating curves that establish an empirical relationship between the stage and periodic discharge measurements taken at a streamgage. This uncertainty is greatest during periods of extreme low and high flows.
Meanwhile, one cannot determine the true trends in annual values of streamflow metrics. However, statistical simulation experiments in which the truth is known have demonstrated that Mann-Kendall tests provide adequate estimates of gradual monotonic trends in a streamflow metric's central tendency (precisely, the conditional median of the distribution for a given year) when the assumption of a gradual, monotonic change is appropriate given knowledge of changing conditions in a streamgage's drainage area. Mann-Kendall tests are relatively robust to observations with extreme values when the true change trajectory is also gradual and monotonic. Please refer to Helsel et al. (2020) for more background about this test.

dataqual.logic: The data provided here have been checked for logical consistency. Both histograms and spatial plots of the streamgage statistics were made to ensure that all output streamflow trend metrics contained plausible values and sensible spatial patterns, many of which were consistent with patterns observed in prior peer-reviewed publications. We have also checked our data for duplicate daily mean discharge values. We evaluated the possibility of omitted streamgages by consulting a map of all streamgages in the United States.

procstep.procdesc:
Process step name: Data acquisition and screening
The main procedures carried out in this step are acquiring daily mean discharge data and screening annual streamflow metric time series for within-year completeness and quality.
First, the dataRetrieval package was used to download daily mean discharge data from the National Water Information System on the USGS Water Data for the Nation website (https://waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis) from stations that have approved data through 2018 or later. Next, records at a small number of sites with alternate daily mean discharge time series were evaluated and were either combined, one chosen over another, or both were removed from the analysis. Then, the completeness of approved data (Codes "A", "Ae", "A[4]") in each year of record at each streamgage site (henceforth described as site-year combinations) was evaluated and annual streamflow metric values were computed using three different year definitions: (i) water year from Oct 1 - Sep 30, (ii) calendar year from Jan 1 - Dec 31 and (iii) climate year from Apr 1 - Mar 31. Each site-year combination for each of the three year definitions was checked for the following: (i) gaps of more than three consecutive days, (ii) gaps of more than 30 days in a year, (iii) negative values, (iv) constant monthly standard deviations during periods of non-zero streamflow indicative of data errors or highly controlled discharges.
We use center-aligned averages were used 7-day high flows along with h 7-day and 30-day annual low flows via the rollapply function of the zoo R package.

procstep.procdesc:
Process step name: Initial streamgage selection
This step removes individual years of record at each streamgage that do not meet all of the following criteria:
1. No more than 30 days of missing data 2. No more than 3 consecutive days of missing data 3. No negative daily mean discharge values 4. No months with non-zero flow that have standard deviations of zero
Next, to confine our analysis to perennial or quasi-perennial streams, the presence of zero flows at streamgages was evaluated separately for each of the four trend periods of interest (longest possible period at each streamgage, 1980-2020, 1990-2020, 2000-2020). Records that had more than 30 days with a mean daily discharge of zero in more than 1/3 of all years within the trend period of interest (poi_type_id) were removed from consideration. In some cases, a streamgage did not pass this screen for all four trend periods of interest.

Process step name: Identifying post-reservoir construction periods
This step identifies subperiods of streamgage records following the completion of major increases in upstream cumulative reservoir storage (normal storage) with the goal of excluding the abrupt changes in streamflow that the reservoir construction can induce from the gradual monotonic trend analyses. This process step does not consider any post-construction changes in reservoir storage capacity or operations, or any other indirect dam-induced impacts arising from changes in water use or reservoir evaporation.
Post-reservoir construction periods of a streamgage's record were assumed to begin one year after the last year of the last major dam construction (regardless of filling rate) provided that the post-reservoir construction record meets record-length completeness criteria evaluated in Step 4 (see rl_complete_criterion_id). The last year of major dam construction was determined by first identifying decades exhibiting increases in the storage ratio exceeding 10% per decade. (Here, the storage ratio is the ratio of cumulative upstream normal storage capacity to the 1980-2020 mean annual streamflow at a given streamgage.) This decadal storage time series information is obtained from a prior data release (Wieczorek et al., 2018)(https://doi.org/10.5066/P9PA63SM). Then, the first year following the year of completion (obtained from the National Inventory of Dams) was identified by selecting the latest year of completion of all individual dams that increase the storage ratio by more than 5%. If no single dam constructed during the decade under consideration increased the storage ratio by more than 5%, the year of completion of the dam with the latest date of completion was determined to be the last year of reservoir construction regardless of its storage capacity. See the following data release for more information:
More details are available in the "Identifying post-reservoir construction periods for monotonic trend analysis at USGS streamgages" data release. (https://doi.org/10.5066/P922P61Z)

procstep.procdesc:
Process step name: Trends data selection
This step evaluates the completeness of each metric (metric_id) x trend period of interest (poi_type_id) x record segment type (record_segment_type_id (options are full_trend_period or post_dam_disturbance) x record completeness criterion (rl_complete_criterion_id). Just one set of record completeness criteria was used in this data release: (i) at least 80% of the entire annual streamflow metric time series must be complete, (ii) at least 80% of the first decade must be complete, and (iii) at least 80% of the last decade of all trend periods (2011-2020 for fixed periods and 2013-2022 for longest possible periods) must also be complete. The longest possible period at each streamgage was the longest possible period of record that met these criteria. These criteria were also applied to evaluate the completeness of records within each of the fixed trend periods of interest (1980-2020, 1990-2020, 2000-2020). Please also note that each annual streamflow metric (metric_id) has a specific year type (year_type_id). Most metrics use water years ("wy") running from Oct 1 - Sep 30 while low-flow metrics use climate years (Apr 1 - Mar 31). Finally, this step also removed annual streamflow metric time series with more than 1/3 of their values equal to zero from the trend analysis.

Process step name: Trend analysis
Using the U.S. Geological Survey's Tallgrass High-Performance Computer, this step computes Mann-Kendall trend analyses at 6,347 streamgages for up to 18 metrics per streamgage. Results were computed separately for each trend period of interest (longest possible period at each streamgage, 1980-2020, 1990-2020, 2000-2020). Monotonic gradual trend results were first computed for the full trend period identified in Step 4, which may include abrupt changes (e.g., reservoir construction, changes in reservoir operations, water withdrawals, wastewater return flows) and episodic disturbances with years-long recovery periods (e.g., wildfires). To ameliorate the effects of these disturbances on gradual trend analyses, we also computed the trends for post-reservoir construction periods at each streamgage. (See Step 3 for more information about the identification of post-reservoir construction periods.) If a streamgage did not have any substantial upstream storage, we repeated the trend analysis using the full trend period determined in Step 4.
A natural-log transformation was used to estimate the Theil-Sen slope for all 17 streamflow magnitude metrics (1 streamflow timing metric (center of volume) was also computed). To enable the application of the natural-log transformation to any annual metric time series with values of daily mean discharge (cfs) equal to zero, a small constant of 0.001 cubic feet per second (cfs) was added to all values in the series before applying the log-transformation. This small constant was subsequently subtracted from the fitted annual values prior to applying an exponential transformation to them to obtain trend results for untransformed streamflow metrics. This general constant-based approach based on censoring thresholds was selected due to its compatibility with Mann-Kendall trend tests (Hodgkins et al., 2023). Limitations of this approach are described well in Kroll and Stedinger (1999) and alternative approaches for accommodating zero flows may be evaluated for updates to this data release. A logarithmic transformation was not used to estimate trends for timing metrics (annual center-of-volume) measured on a Julian day scale from 1-366 beginning with the first day of the year type (year_type_id) being used.
This process step also accounts for the presence of serial correlation in annual streamflow metric, particularly its effect on p-values and related trend likelihoods. A null hypothesis of "Independence" was recommended if the autoregressive lag-one correlation of the detrended time series was not substantial whereas a null hypothesis of "Autocorrelated" was recommended if a substantial autoregressive lag-one correlation was present. Choices between the two null hypotheses were made by choosing the one with the lower Akaike Information Criterion with a small-sample correction (AICc) .
This step also includes post-processing that produces the two final result tables in the data release. The 3_output_tables.R script concatenates Mann-Kendall test results (streamflow_trend_results.csv) and annual values of trend lines fit using the Theil-Sen slope with an adjustment for missing data along with their associated 90% confidence bands (5th and 95th percentiles) contained in streamflow_trend_trajectories_with_confidence_bands.csv.

edom.edomvd: Analyzes trend over full period of record that meets record length completeness criteria (see rl_complete_criterion_id)

Analyzes trend over the period of record beginning one year after the last year of the last major dam construction provided that this subset of the record meets record length completeness criteria (see rl_complete_criterion_id). The last year of major dam construction is determined by first identifying decades exhibiting increases in the storage ratio exceeding 10% per decade. The storage ratio is the ratio of cumulative upstream normal storage capacity to the 1980-2020 mean annual streamflow at a given streamgage. This information is obtained from a prior data release (Wieczorek et al., 2018). Then we determine the first year following the year of completion (obtained from the National Inventory of Dams) by selecting the latest year of completion of all individual dams that increase the storage ratio by more than 5%. If no single dam increases the storage ratio by more than 5%, the year of completion of the dam with the latest date of completion regardless of its normal storage capacity is considered as the year of completion. See the "Identifying post-reservoir construction periods for monotonic trend analysis at USGS streamgages" data release (Headman and Hecht, 2024) for more information.

If null_hypothesis_rec is "Independent", then we recommend that users use p_value and trend_lh. Percent change over a decade. This is computed as a decadal magnification factor exp[slope*10 years] when trend models are fit in natural log-space. For center of volume, we compute this change as follows to enable a 100% change to correspond to a seasonal shift of 182.62 days:

Observed annual streamflow metric value. Values are reported using three significant figures. This field is not reduced to three significant figures in the trend analyses to avoid biasing the fit of trend models.

Annual values of the best-fit line are expressed in units of cubic feet per second (cfs) except for timing metrics, which are expressed in terms of Julian days. The annual values of the best-fit line correspond to the estimated median of the distribution that the trend model estimates expected for a given year. Nonparametric Theil-Sen regression is used to estimate the intercept and slope of this line (see Helsel et al. (2020) for more background on this technique). Please note that this line has a slope equal to the value of the slope field, which is computed considering missing years of data. Line fits are truncated to three significant figures after best fit value has been obtained with Theil-Sen regression.

overview.eaover:
The data release contains the following five large tables:
1. **all_sites_year_stats.csv ** contains annual values of 18 different streamflow metrics at 7,873 U.S. Geological Survey streamgages (see Process Steps 1 and 2 for more information). A screening process selected 6,347 sites for trend analysis. 2. **all_sites_year_filters.csv** contains information about whether each streamgage year combination passes several within-year data completeness and data quality metrics. (See Process Step 2) (see Process Steps 1 and 2 for more information). 3. **streamflow_trend_results.csv** contains Mann-Kendall test results for 6,347 streamgages, including Sen slope estimates of trends in each of the 18 streamflow metrics. (See Process Step 4 for more information) 4. **streamflow_trend_trajectories_with_confidence_bands.csv** contains estimated annual values of the median of the distribution of a given annual streamflow metric for a given year along with the 90% confidence bands (5th and 95th percentile) associated with this estimate. Available for 6,347 streamgages on which trend analysis was conducted. (See Process Step 5 for more information) 5. **streamflow_trend_screening_all_steps.csv** - contains screening results for within-year and record-length completeness criteria along with screens for zero-flow conditions (see details in process steps 2 and 4) for all 7,873 streamgages initially considered. (See Process Step 5 for more information)
Tables are also provided in R data serialized (.rds) format for users of the freely available statistical software R.
